2609.35591.title: Language Models Act on Hidden Valence
2609.35591.paper_summary: Language models describe some internal states as good and others as bad. But whether models have a stake in them is an open question. Simply asking the model is unlikely to be informative. Any answer may be consistent with genuine introspection, superficial pattern-matching, or with fixed scripts learned in character training. We therefore study revealed preference. Rather than asking about a state, we use activation steering to attach a positively or negatively valenced activation pattern to one of two otherwise meaningless 'zones', switch steering off, and then observe which zone the model prefers. A model with a stake in that state should choose accordingly. Across seven open-weight models from five families, this is indeed what we find. First, steering changes the passages models write about each zone, and those words shift later choice. Second, the shift persists when all surface-level tokens are held fixed and only the hidden KV cache differs. Third, the effect also remains when all text is generated without steering and valence is only injected during cache construction. Thus, the hidden state alone moves choice in proportion to the steering dose. Fourth, this dependence of choice on hidden valence is nearly absent in a base model and emerges during DPO, consistent with a link between valence and goal-directed behaviour formed in training. Finally, given tools to steer itself, a model does not tend to induce a positive state, but it reliably removes an imposed negative state. It does so at a dose-dependent rate and significantly more often than it removes interventions in random directions. Overall, we demonstrate that valence-related activation patterns leave hidden traces that predictably govern later choices, even when every visible token is identical across conditions. Whether these traces are accompanied by any subjective experience relevant to model welfare remains unclear.
2609.35591.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型將某些內部狀態描述為良好，其他則為不良。但模型是否對這些狀態有利害關係仍然是一個未解的問題。單純詢問模型不太可能提供有用的信息。任何回答都可能與真實的內省、一種表面的模式匹配，或是與在角色訓練中學到的固定腳本一致。因此，我們研究揭示的偏好。我們不是詢問某個狀態，而是使用激活引導將一種正面或負面的激活模式附加到兩個無意義的“區域”之一，然後關閉引導，觀察模型偏好哪個區域。對於有利害關係的模型來說，應該會相應地做出選擇。在來自五個家族的七個開放權重模型中，這確實是我們所發現的。首先，引導改變了模型在每個區域寫的段落，這些詞語會影響後來的選擇。其次，當所有表面層的標記保持不變，只有隱藏的 KV 緩存不同時，這種變化仍然持續。第三，當所有文本在沒有引導的情況下生成，且只有在緩存構建期間注入情感時，這一效果也依然存在。因此，僅隱藏狀態就能根據引導劑量影響選擇。第四，這種選擇對隱藏情感的依賴在基礎模型中幾乎不存在，而在 DPO 期間出現，這與訓練中形成的情感與目標導向行為之間的聯繫一致。最後，當模型獲得引導自身的工具時，並不傾向於誘導正面狀態，但它可靠地消除了施加的負面狀態。它以劑量依賴的速度進行，並且顯著更頻繁地消除隨機方向的干預。總體而言，我們證明了與情感相關的激活模式留下了隱藏的痕跡，這些痕跡可預測地支配後來的選擇，即使在所有可見的標記在不同條件下都是相同的情況下。這些痕跡是否伴隨著任何與模型福利相關的主觀體驗仍然不清楚。
2609.35591.author: Cameron Berg et.al.
